verifier_notes: Every url re-opened. Campaign sites read with the kit's own downloader (WebFetch's lookups failed for several hosts; the router's lost lookups, not the sites).

The State Election Board's results site (results.okelections.us) answers scripts with 403, so the five 2024 past_party entries were checked against the official county results file saved from that site (ballot_cache/ok/place_votes/20241105/20241105_CountyResults_csv.zip): every row matches race, name and cand_party. Nothing was worked around; the link is kept for readers, whose browsers it serves.
Towns of residence printed in the 2024 officer roster were taken out of the source quotes.
notes: Ages printed by news sources (Eastman 53, Sullivan 41, Stokes 57, Hassink 69, Pena 30) were not turned into birth years: an age alone fits two years.

past_party entries come from the State Election Board's own results: the certified 2022 summary in the Board's meeting packet of November 15, 2022 (pages 11 and 13 print each candidate with the party), and the official results site for November 5, 2024 (which refuses scripts; the precinct and county files John saved from it, ballot_cache/ok/place_votes/20241105/20241105_CountyResults_csv.zip, carry the same rows with cand_party).

Sitting legislators (Lawson, Rosecrants, Blair, Kelley, McCane, West, Brooks): only a campaign website was looked for. michaelforoklahoma.com, linked for Brooks by the Oklahoma Democratic Party, only forwards to an ActBlue page, so it is not recorded. gilmoreforok.com, linked for Gilmore by Blue Voter Guide, is a parked domain today.
No Oklahoma party page read calls anything an endorsement for a 2026 state or local race (see ballot/lean/ok_endorsements.json), so endorsed_by is empty throughout.
